Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: onboarding and first-run activation.

## Why
The activation funnel now measures signup → first project → first successful build → first publish (`lib/events.ts`, rendered on `/admin`). Nothing is designed to move people through it. A new account lands on a dashboard with a seed project and no guidance about what to do or what a credit is.

## Read first (all READ ONLY unless listed in scope)
- `lib/events.ts` — the funnel and the North Star (first PUBLISH, not signup).
- `lib/seed-project.ts` and `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` — what a new account already gets.
- `lib/pending-prompt.ts`, `app/continue/**` — how a prompt typed before signup survives into a project.
- `lib/templates.ts` and `app/templates/` — a 23-template gallery exists; the nav now links to it. **Complement it, do not duplicate it.**
- `lib/enhance.ts` — auto-enhance already exists.
- `lib/credits.ts` — `SIGNUP_GRANT` is 750. Measured builds have cost 144 and 472 credits, so that is **under two builds**. Onboarding must not imply otherwise.

## Build
1. **A first-run experience on the dashboard for an account with no builds yet** — a compact, dismissible checklist tied to the real funnel steps (create a site → describe it → publish it), each reflecting actual state, not a static list. It must disappear once they're past it and never nag.
2. **Explain credits honestly, once.** What a credit is, that the grant is 750, that failed builds are free, and that the spend cap exists. Do **not** state a per-build cost — measurements are 144 and 472, a threefold spread, and `estimateCredits`'s own comment says that is not a distribution.
3. **A "not sure what to type?" path** from the empty state to `/templates`, and a pointer to Enhance for people who have typed something rough.
4. **Progressive, not blocking.** No modal wall, no forced tour, nothing that stands between someone and their first build. The board has an explicit card: "Never force the wizard — raw box stays the default." Respect it.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `components/onboarding/**`, `app/continue/**`
You may NOT edit `app/dashboard/page.tsx` — another agent's territory and it is being changed. Build your components so a single import + one line renders them, and **state that exact line in your report** so I can wire it.

## Constraints
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/dashboard/** (except as noted: nothing), app/projects/**, app/settings/**, app/admin/**, app/templates/**, app/globals.css, components/marketing/**, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- **Dismissal state**: you cannot add a schema field. Derive "are they past this step?" from real data (projects, builds, `publishedAt`) rather than storing a flag, or use `localStorage` for the dismissal only — and say which you chose and why.
- Match the dashboard idiom: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, monochrome.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast; known accepted issue).
- Accessibility bar: real labels, visible `focus-visible:` states, no keyboard traps, no horizontal scroll at 380px, `aria-*` on stateful controls.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

## Report back
What you built, the exact import + JSX line to wire it into the dashboard, how you derived progress and dismissal, what you verified, and any claim about cost you deliberately avoided.

- hyperframes: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.
- hyperframes-audio: Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), or automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter. Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.
- hyperframes-cli: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.
- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.

For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.
- hyperframes-keyframes: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

## What I built

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\onboarding\FirstRunChecklist.tsx`** — async server component, zero props. It calls `getCurrentUser()` itself and runs four cheap queries in parallel (published-project count, project count, `SUCCEEDED` build count, most-recently-updated project). Returns `null` if signed out, or if any project has `publishedAt` set.

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\onboarding\FirstRunPanel.tsx`** — the `"use client"` presentation + dismissal shell, plus a `CreditPrimer` sub-component in the same file.

The card is a compact `<section>` in the dashboard idiom (`rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, monochrome, no gradients anywhere — so no new white-on-gradient text). Three `<ol>` rows mirroring the funnel in `lib/events.ts`: create a site → describe it and build it → publish it. Completed rows collapse to a dimmed title with a check; only outstanding rows show body copy. Header reads "N of 3 done · your first published site is the finish line".

Templates/Enhance path lives in step 2's body: "Not sure what to type? **Start from one of {TEMPLATES.length} written prompts**" linking `/templates` (count imported, not hardcoded — currently 23), followed by "Already typed something rough? Press **Enhance** next to the box — it expands your line into a fuller spec you can read and edit first, and it costs no credits." It points at the existing gallery rather than duplicating any of it.

An "Open {project name}" shortcut appears only while a project exists but no build has succeeded — it disappears once it would just be a worse copy of the project list.

## Exact wiring line

```tsx
import FirstRunChecklist from "@/components/onboarding/FirstRunChecklist";
```

```tsx
<FirstRunChecklist />
```

Drop it in `app/dashboard/page.tsx` between the account header block and the `<div className="mb-6 flex items-center justify-between">` "Your sites" row. It carries its own `mb-6`, needs no props, and renders nothing when it shouldn't. It's an async server component, so it has to sit in the server tree (the dashboard page already is one).

## Progress and dismissal

**Progress: fully derived, no schema field, no stored flag.** Step 1 = a project exists (the signup seed counts — it is a real project, so a new account sees 1 of 3 already done, which is true rather than flattering). Step 2 = `db.build.count({ where: { project: { userId }, status: "SUCCEEDED" } }) > 0`. Step 3 = a project with non-null `publishedAt`, which is also the exit condition — reaching the North Star makes the panel vanish permanently, with nothing to write and nothing to reset. A build that succeeded in another tab or a publish from another device is reflected on next load; a progress column would have drifted the first time anything happened outside this component.

**Dismissal: `localStorage` only**, key `kodely:first-run-dismissed`. Reasoning: "I don't want to see this" is a per-device UI preference, not a fact about the account, so it doesn't deserve a column even if I could add one; losing it on another device is harmless, whereas losing derived progress would not be.

It's read through `useSyncExternalStore` rather than state-synced in an effect. Three consequences worth knowing: the ESLint rule `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` (which is an *error* in this config, not a warning) is satisfied; the server snapshot is "dismissed", so the panel is never server-rendered and then yanked away a frame later for someone who already closed it — it fades in just after hydration instead; and dismissing in one tab hides it in the others via the `storage` event. A module-level `dismissedThisSession` fallback keeps the button working where `localStorage` throws (private mode, full quota).

## The cost claim I deliberately avoided

**No per-build credit cost anywhere** — no average, no "typical build", not even `estimateCredits`' 120–550 range. Two measurements 3x apart (144 and 472) are not a distribution, as that function's own comment says, and inventing precision is the exact failure the credits module exists to prevent. Instead "what will this cost me?" is answered by pointing at the `CreditMeter` already at the top of the dashboard, which is computed from that person's own build history.

What the primer *does* state, all sourced from `lib/credits.ts` rather than retyped: a credit is real model spend and 500 credits is $1 (derived at render time from `MICROS_PER_CREDIT`, so it can't drift); the account starts with 750 (`SIGNUP_GRANT`, passed as a prop); failed and stopped builds are charged nothing; a rolling-30-day spend cap can be set in Settings, with a link. The grant is framed as "enough to get a first site built and iterate on it. How far it goes after that depends on how much you ask for" — it never implies many builds.

## Progressive, not blocking

Inline card, no modal, no tour, no focus trap, no autofocus. Nothing sits between anyone and the raw prompt box, and every step is a description of state plus an optional shortcut. It's dismissible at any time and it never re-appears once dismissed or once they publish.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean across the repo.
- `npx eslint app lib components` — clean, zero errors and zero warnings (the pre-existing `admin/audit` type error and the unused-import warnings in `lib/rate-limit.ts` I saw mid-session were resolved by other agents; nothing outstanding now).
- Accessibility by inspection: `aria-labelledby` on the section; `aria-label` on the dismiss button; `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` on the credits toggle, with the target kept mounted (`hidden` attribute) so `aria-controls` always resolves; `sr-only` "— done" on completed steps since the check mark is `aria-hidden`; `focus-visible:ring-2` on every link and button, matching the constant `app/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx` uses (redefined locally rather than imported, to avoid coupling to a file another agent is editing); native semantics throughout, so no keyboard trap.
- 380px by inspection: no fixed widths, no `whitespace-nowrap`, `min-w-0` on every flexed text container, and `min-w-0 truncate` on the project-name button so a long name can't push the card past the viewport.

## `app/continue/**`

Left untouched. Note that the route actually lives at `app/(auth)/continue/page.tsx`, not `app/continue/` — creating the latter would register a second page resolving to `/continue` and break the route. Nothing in the four build items required a change there: the pending-prompt hand-off already works end to end (`PromptHero`/`TemplateGallery` stash → signup/login/`/continue` call `destinationAfterAuth()` → `Editor` fires the first build on mount).
